payout_quote: The current service fee is 20%, and the service fee amount will be shown transparently to you on each booking request you receive.
steps: Submit your space on Peerspace: create a host account, describe the space with photos, set your own hourly price, availability, and house rules.
Pass Peerspace's listing review (typically within 1 hour during standard business hours) and optimize your listing.
Receive booking requests with a transparent breakdown (license charge, Peerspace service fee, your expected payout); accept or decline each request.
Host the booking (events, meetings, photo/film shoots); payout is processed within 7 days of the booking date for the license charge minus the 20% service fee.
catches: Peerspace takes a 20% service fee from hosts on the booking amount plus any additional fees you charge guests (cleaning, add-ons) - the highest host cut in this lane; older marketing materials said 15% but the current official Support Center figure is 20%.

Earnings are fully variable: you set the hourly rate but income depends on how unique/photogenic your space is, location, and demand; 'majority of spaces go for $100-$250/hour' is a market observation, not a guarantee - most spaces get few or no bookings.
Peerspace's $1M host insurance is supplemental general liability: you must still maintain your own primary commercial liability policy per their own terms.
Some markets are US-only; available in US, UK, and Canada - check your city is covered before investing setup time.

Productions and events bring strangers into your property: damage, overtime, and neighbor/HOA complaints are your operational risk; you must review the Cancellation and Refund policy before accepting.
Rental income is taxable; also check local venue/event permitting, noise rules, and HOA/lease restrictions.
Bookings can be cancelled per the cancellation policy - a confirmed booking is not guaranteed income until the event happens.
biggest_catch: Peerspace keeps 20% of every booking (plus guest-side processing fees) and there is no guaranteed income: bookings depend entirely on how unique your space is and local demand, most spaces get few or no bookings, and you must carry your own primary commercial liability policy since Peerspace's $1M coverage is only supplemental.
eligibility: US, UK, or Canada. Must be 18+, own or control the space (or have written approval), meet Peerspace listing quality requirements, and maintain a primary commercial liability insurance policy. Comply with local event/venue, noise, and permitting rules.
timing: Listing submission and review is quick (review typically within 1 hour in business hours); hosts are typically paid within 3-7 days of the booking date via direct deposit. First booking can take weeks or months of zero earnings.
weasel_words: fill your calendar and bank account
